parts.title: What you are looking at
parts.summary: A quantum computer is a stack: a program, timed hardware operations, firmware for control processors, wires, and the qubits at the end. Learn to read every layer of one run.

lessons.title: The stack in one picture
lessons.hook: A three-line program becomes 400 events on 24 parts. Follow it from the source line to the qubit.

lessons.title: Batches: the clock everything runs on
lessons.hook: Every time in the machine is a whole number of clock cycles. Find out how long one is, and why.

lessons.title: Following one pulse
lessons.hook: One store instruction, one link, one queue, one DAC, one coax, one qubit. Walk the causal chain.

lessons.title: Reading the workspace
lessons.hook: Four synchronized layers and a 3D stage. Learn which question each one answers.

parts.title: Programming the controller
parts.summary: The control processor does not play pulses; it schedules them ahead of time through memory-mapped registers. Learn the mechanism that makes timing exact.

lessons.title: Posted writes and the pulse table
lessons.hook: A pulse is a row in a table. Firing it is one store to one address.

lessons.title: Timed queues and the lead
lessons.hook: Issue early, land exactly. Why the firmware works 96 cycles in the future.

lessons.title: Measurement results come back
lessons.hook: A demodulation window, a decoder pipeline and a load that stalls until the bit is ready.

lessons.title: Cores meet: the board hub
lessons.hook: Shared bits, barriers and mailboxes, one message per cycle for the whole board.

parts.title: Three machines, one controller
parts.summary: Superconducting qubits, trapped ions and neutral atoms differ in physics but share one control problem. See how the same controller drives each.

lessons.title: Superconducting: from OpenQASM to microwaves
lessons.hook: Gates become calibrated microwave pulses, virtual Z becomes a phase, and readout is a tone plus a window.

lessons.title: Trapped ions: shuttling is a waveform
lessons.hook: An ion moves because electrode voltages change. Every hop is a burst of DAC waveforms.

lessons.title: Neutral atoms: tones carry atoms
lessons.hook: An acousto-optic deflector turns an RF frequency into a position. Step the frequency and the atom follows.

lessons.title: The same controller everywhere
lessons.hook: Compare the three runs: what changes, what stays, and what limits each.

parts.title: Designing hardware
parts.summary: A machine is a document: parts, positions, channels and routed wires, checked against rules. Change the hardware and watch the timing change.

lessons.title: A machine is a document
lessons.hook: Parts, channels, wires and calibrations: read the design of an eight-qubit ring.

lessons.title: Wire length is latency
lessons.hook: Move the chip two metres away and every pulse arrives 10 ns later. Nothing at the converters changes.

lessons.title: Who drives what
lessons.hook: Give three qubits to one core and the feed-forward never touches the hub.

lessons.title: When a design breaks a rule
lessons.hook: Converters of the wrong kind, wires that end nowhere, readouts that return too late.

parts.title: Fault tolerance on the controller
parts.summary: Error correction needs measurements, decoding and corrections within a deadline. Measure what the control system costs, and run a real decoder on a control core.

lessons.title: Feedback latency
lessons.hook: From the end of a readout window to the conditioned pulse: every nanosecond accounted for.

lessons.title: System calls
lessons.hook: measure, decode_syndrome, pauli_frame_update: a fault-tolerant program as calls on the controller.

lessons.title: A real decoder on a control core
lessons.hook: The C union-find of the Helios decoder, compiled for RISC-V and checked against its own test vectors.

lessons.title: Limits: bandwidth, concurrency, depth
lessons.hook: How many bits per microsecond, how many pulses at once, how deep a link. Find where a schedule stops fitting.

background.title: Qubits and what controls them
background.summary: Transmons, trapped ions and neutral atoms: what a qubit is in each, and which signals act on it.

background.title: Classical control systems
background.summary: FPGAs, DACs, ADCs, numerically controlled oscillators, clocks, cables and optics.

background.title: The RISC-Q architecture
background.summary: One RISC-V core per channel group, posted writes, pulse tables, timed queues, sinks and the board hub.

background.title: Deterministic timing
background.summary: Why control systems schedule ahead, what the lead covers, and what the Lean proofs guarantee.

background.title: Measurement, feedback and decoding
background.summary: Readout, feed-forward, syndromes, decoders and the deadline every error-correction round must meet.

background.title: How this simulator works
background.summary: Lowering, firmware, the Lean model, the trace, and what is proved, tested or assumed.

background.title: Numbers and sources
background.summary: Every latency, duration and rate the simulator uses, with where it comes from.

background.title: Glossary
background.summary: Every term of the course, in one sentence each.
